items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: This man, Aaron, had his own cab stand, had his own restaurant, and had his own meat shop.

ctx.x: When did you start playing music professionally for, you know, your first few jobs?

Well I wasn't calling myself a professional before, before 24. I was in ninth grade, 35, right there, F1-0. And these two guys was taking lessons. This man and these guys were married men and everything. They left in the days first. The Trammer played George Morris, and Trump was played Thomas Mack. And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington. I just buried them this year, first part of this year. And they used to get a little job, they used to hire me. They had family and everything. I mean, they were work guys,…
Yeah. So you decided pretty much in Pensacola that, or?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: we had this particular man, Aaron Long, I forgot to tell you. He booked us on a trip

ctx.x: So, uh, we stayed around there, I'd say, uh... Oh, let's see. I came back here, it was just before 27. Uh-huh. Well, the band made a big hit. Uh-huh. And we didn't have no particular man, we had this particular man, Aaron Long, I forgot to tell you. He booked us on a trip, he gave up his market, and booked us on a trip from Pensacola to Jacksonville. And the fellow, George Morris, we were not talking to Aaron Long, talking to the band members, he said, if we get to Jacksonville, he said, I know if we get down to…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: the guy that was under Meatmark was named Mary and Long

ctx.x: So we left. We went to Pensacola, Florida. And when we got there, we took up a piano player. I can't think of the woman's name right now. And we played for a doctor named. There was two fellas running a baseball park there. There was one, Dr. Burgundy, and the guy that was under Meatmark was named Mary and Long. It was sort of a corporation. They ran this baseball park with named Moore Castle Park. And they had a colored ball team. We used to play like Mobile and Montgomery all around that vicinity.
But did you always play guitar in the early days or did you play banjo as well?
